title: Bounding Box and Partial Update
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Bounding Box
Partial Screen Update
OLED
Animation
description: Compare a full redraw with a partial update on an OLED clock by counting the pixels each one redraws when the seconds change.

educational.topic: Bounding boxes and partial screen updates
learningObjectives: Analyze how erasing one bounding box updates part of the screen without disturbing the rest
Compare the pixels redrawn by a full redraw and a partial update
Explain why show() still sends the whole buffer on the OLED
prerequisites: Drawing shapes and text with framebuf (Chapter 12)

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Comparison of two strategies on the same data
keyQuestions: Why must the old box be erased before drawing the new seconds?
When does a partial update redraw more than one box?
What would happen if two bounding boxes overlapped?
commonMisconceptions: A partial update makes show() faster on the OLED (show() still sends the whole buffer)
You can draw new digits over old ones without erasing (the digits smear together)
assessmentOpportunities: The student computes the seconds box area as 16 x 8 = 128 pixels.
The student explains that items whose boxes do not overlap the changed one are untouched.
The student states that the bus still carries 1,024 bytes per show().
